title: Suzhou silk embroidery (Su xiu)
summary: Su xiu is the silk embroidery of Suzhou, in eastern China. Makers split silk floss into hair-fine strands and lay them in flat, even stitches, shifting direction and shade so petals, leaves and birds look soft and round.
howToPlay: Pick a silk colour from the spools and a stitch from the tray beside the frame.
Touch a square on the silk to work that stitch there; it is mirrored on the other half of the cloth.
Copy the sketch shown beside the frame, then press Check.
rules: The design is mirrored left and right, so each stitch you place is also worked on its partner square.
A square counts only when its stitch and its silk colour both match the sketch you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Su xiu has been made in and around Suzhou for well over a thousand years and is counted among the great regional embroidery styles of China. Embroiderers still train for years to master its split threads and fine, even stitching.
